en: The *Sāmaveda* has seven characteristics:
the *śamana*,
the vowel *ā* preceded by a protracted (*pluta*) vowel and followed by a voiced consonant;
Furthermore, when followed by the letter *śa*, the *visarga* is elided;
we shall now explain those words here according to the *saṃhitā* of the *ṛc*s.
Sonant consonants include the letter *ha* and the letters *ga*, *ja*, *ḍa*, and so forth.
The technical rules (paribhāṣā) are as follows: "dādayo bādayo vānta yājayo'nyayujau śasau" (2).
The others are: vidā, muni, stomā, devā, rudrā, na, martya, vardhe, deve, vasu, mayobhu, taye, śaram, pracetā, anūdhāḥ, pṛthivyā, bhūtan, nasṛṇi, taye, dhiyam, dhā, viśva, ṛyugam.

He does not [conceal] the eyes from hatred; assuming forms, he, the bearer of wealth, the leader around, has made the forms and riches manifest. Having become the ear, O most powerful one, you have made the abodes manifest for the donor, O Soma. And you, O Yugma, having looked upon our earthly worlds and blessings, have established the regions of heaven. At the time of the *ṛkṣara*, Jātavedas was the first of the weapons of Yugma;

the whips were desired, and the Somas, acting in concert, made the path. Like yoked horses, they did not fail at the time of growth; those which are most honey-sweet, O Rudras, are the living ones—the second [group].
That which the noble ones, seeking it, regard as the eye that creates the world at the end of the Veda;
which the armies, vying with one another, behold as shining and wise at the end of the sacrifice;
which is revealed by the debt-payers, dwelling together, piled up like the offspring of the Cow—the third [is this].
The sages, protectors of the jewels, are worthy of the eye-faculty; they do not let the progeny fall from the Veda, O Child, at the onset.
A hundred streams flow like rain; the blind man does not follow behind the son.
Yearning for protection, the friends are bright; the well-milking cows form a pair, and the fourth is the dawn. 6.10.6.1–4.
Then those others, the most recent arrivals, have come like horses at the time of their whinnying; O you who bestow splendor upon the sea, you flow forth as the fifth of all.
(7) The fierce, firm ones, terrifying and devouring, have been placed for you; being cleansed, they win the horse through their power, resounding as the sixth. (8)
Like those being praised for the sake of the one who does not falter, for these flowing ones are indeed swift steeds; and these Soma-drinkers, while being purified, have the eye as their seventh.

(9) Free from sin, knowing the path, wise, free from disease, unknown to affliction, having cast off all obstacles, they are the first to grant aid, dear in their union for the sake of the one who does not falter.

With good guardians, god-seeking, ruddy-colored, and performing sacrifice—may they, born of power, may they, the fierce conquerors, the unassailable youths of far-reaching fame, be our eighth against the enemies. (10)
It is said that there were indeed numerical sūtras in the Śamānaka;
for there are examples ranging from one up to Rudra (eleven).
Among those, however, the six, the eight Vasus, the powers (Śaktis), and the ten are not seen.
And by the method of one [thread] alone, seventy-nine extractions are taught (12).
By means of two [threads] for one [thread], the number of Rudras is stated here;
and for one thread alone, a triad is proclaimed (13).
Clearly, there exist three groups of sūtras numbering as many as the Vedas;
indeed, one group of sūtras numbering as many as the elements is certain.
Furthermore, the number of sūtras numbering as many as the sages is proclaimed to be equal to the number of eyes.
Among the locations numbered as eleven (the number of Rudras), only one is proclaimed [as primary].

15. Those who know that one among these is devoid of number understand it to be the elemental state of tranquility; thus the illustration has been clearly stated by way of number, though it is essentially beyond being.
"In the Sūtras themselves, however, the elision (*visarga*) is subject to the prohibition of the ten positions" (16). Thus ends the section on the elision and non-elision of *visarga*.
Regarding the rule proclaimed for those [sāmans] whose *svāra* occurs in the middle, we state here by way of illustration that it does not apply to others in this case:
"O Lord of the earth, protect us from every enemy. (17–18)

Likewise, one should observe such passages as: "Thus at dawn, even without ritual action, he was brought forth; he was established above the funeral pyre; he obstructed [the waters] among the Nahuṣī rivers," and so forth. 19.
Raṅga.
The *raṅga* (nasal) should be known as twofold; it is said to be either following a vowel or following a consonant. Its definition and illustration are clearly stated [as follows]:
here, the modification of the letter *na*, which is nasal (*nāsikya*), is called *raṅga*.

In the middle of a word, at the end of a word, and before a vowel, [the substitution] is "kalaśām̐" (21). Before a consonant suffix, whatever the color (raṅga) may be, by that there is the illustration:
"dāśivām̐ vaḥ", "atha gomām̐ yaḥ", "dadhanvām̐ yaḥ", and "yo mahām̐ hi ṣaḥ" (22).
Having crossed over and bowed to the goddess Bhāratī, the sole mother of all the worlds,
I shall proclaim Nārāyaṇa and the verses that are to be crossed over. 23
Those words ending in the phonemes *e* and *ai*, which undergo modification in *saṃhitā*, are declared by the best knowers of the Veda to be "viliṅghya.
Having omitted what is redundant in the ancient [text] and having added what was left unsaid, [the text is thus corrected]. 24.
Those [words] are indeed grasped by means of the Ṛk-grammar together with its commentary.
Whatever word is to be grasped as a cause is grasped precisely as that word;
even if there were another [word], it is not prescribed here for the purpose of filling out the meter.
O Agni, you grow strong when cooked by Kaṇva; this is for you, and day after day it is yours.
These two are heard of as a refuge in the great contest; I have fashioned these songs at the shared feast. This is your first [offering] for your brilliance.

For you, the ocean-like one, the Soma is poured out; I sprinkle it for the beloved pair, for the sacrifice, for the host of gods. We invoke the Lord of Power with our vision for the drinking; he has yoked himself for the exhilaration. He is renowned for his arms; they hold back [the enemies] for the drinking of Soma. You have left behind the second [state]. 28.

In the desire for sustenance, we worship Bharaṇī and Śūla; in the midst of the turning of the eye, Trita is praised. O Lord of Cows, you purify yourself and strive for our well-being as the third (29).
For the sake of great and beloved speech, while being impelled, he is the fourth (30).

For the singer, for increase, you place [the prize] in the vessel; for the giver of good gifts on the chariot, you lead the yoking for the winning of booty, so that splendor may be seen, he is invoked for the feast of the gods—he purifies himself as the fifth (31).

O you who move among all people, O pillar, you are invoked; you are mixed [with offerings], O Lord. We prepare a pair for the impetuous Sun, for the sake of hearing. They yoke [the horses] for the one who is kindled; those who carry the pair in the woolly fleece increase in the pit, in the house, and in the form. They speak and they bathe [the victim] at the sacrifice. The sixth [verse]: "In the jar he has swelled; they purify themselves for the bull to see; he has rained upon the forest; he was born in the vicinity. I have spoken; they have restrained themselves for help. At midday, the sound is found. The seventh [verse]. The *ekāraviliṅghya* section is completed.

To praise, to cross by means of a raft, to overcome the crocodile, to slay, to gain, to flow, to attain all, and to reach—that is for him, for this one worthy of guidance; thus ends the eighth [section], 34.
The letter *ai* is completed; now, having counted the *viliṅghya-sūtra*, it is designated as the Kali [period].

Indeed, he states the examples ranging from one up to five: "For the fifteenth [day], there is one; and for the twenty-fourth, there is one; and for the first, it is likewise stated that the number of dhama-s follows this same method. (35–36)
Just as the number of heaps is stated by taking one as two, so too it is determined that the number of arrows is proclaimed by taking a single thread as two. 37.
Thus, among the threads numbering as many as the arrows, one [thread] is thus celebrated.
The direct citation has been declared, and the enumeration known as Kali has been stated [in thirty-eight verses].
38. They know that, excluding one among these, the material [portion] is transgressed by the number; and the sūtras of the vowel *ai* are said to be ten in number. 39.
In one case, by a single method, the number of treasures (vasu) is thus stated;
in another case, by way of duality, the number of hands is thus stated; the illustrative example is declared by means of an equalization with the number of the heap (rāśi). 40.
The *Viliṅghya* is completed;
having bowed to the supreme deity Vināyaka, who bestows all prosperity, who is neither beyond nor not beyond.
The son of Śauri shall proclaim the new supreme state (pada) for those who bow; and I shall establish the characteristics of the first supreme name,
which is difficult to understand, difficult to recite, dependent [on context], and likewise lacking in proper sequence.
Having set that aside, he composed an extensive commentary;
yet some argue that this [work] should not be undertaken because it is already established by itself through well-known study. 43. Regarding that, some are greatly perplexed.
How is it determined by certain skillful and noble-souled ones?
(44) It is determined through a characteristic corresponding to itself;
at first, these two are subject to modification, for their scope does not extend beyond this point. (45)
Those two alone are the subject matter (*abhidheya*), and the knowledge thereof is the purpose (*prayojana*).
When the four [consonants] beginning with *cha*—excluding the letter *tha*—and the letter *ma* and the letter *la* stand as subsequent [sounds], [the following rule applies]. 46.

I shall explain the words so that one may recognize those in which a *vikārin* (subject to change) is seen at the end of a word, whether it be the letter *t* followed by *na*, or otherwise. First, I will list the words ending in *t* according to the sequence beginning with the vowel *a*.
Then, by this very sequence, that which ends in the letter *takāra* is grasped; thus is the technical rule (*paribhāṣā*). [The verse continues:
"O great one, O you who know the sky, do not sit upon the seat; do not [neglect] me, O great one, when others are present."
O wondrous god, come to our sacrifice like a treasure for us who seek the gods;
may the lord of bay horses, Maghavan, come to us with his steeds and grant us ninefold wealth that brings prosperity. May the gods come to us with their protections. 49–50.
Like a great friend, chanting like a measured song, he goes to his dwelling; bestowing waters for exhilaration, the Son beholds all births and, like one who restrains,
he has spread out these worlds and made them shine.
When he was placed therein, crying out, the gods generated the honey;
like a wave, O wise ones, the Soma flowed over the enemies in his exhilaration.
In that intoxication, the Dasyus perished by their own bodies, and the great earth trembled all around.

Shining brightly, O light, exhilarate the gods; go forth like a lover, driving away misfortunes with your flowing stream, you who are most intoxicating. 54. May the honeyed drop, the sustainer of the law, likewise cause the heavens to blaze.
O Maghavan, a word ending in 'na' is proclaimed to be a *pada* only when it is not followed by another [word]; thus,
the rules concerning what follows 'na' (*napara*) have been concluded, and the number of *sūtras* regarding *napara* is said to be equal to that of the throat (*galasaṃkhyā*).

In this manner, many numbers are described as being of a single type for a single entity (verse 56). Likewise, the number one is described by means of duality for a single entity; thus, the illustrative example is stated by way of comparison with the number of trees (verse 57).
Thus the *napara* [section] is completed;
now follows the *tapara-sandhi*:
"O Mother, since you have a son, know [him] by yourself; O Arcin, you are not to be despised."
Some have been bound by the noose-holders, and likewise, O Maghavan, some here have been made to rest;
that [power] of yours has reached us, and it shall reach us again and again; O finder of wealth, grant that to us.
O Soma, in that intoxication, you struck down that great being with your power of illusion;
even as we are here, so now, O Purifier, may this [sacrifice] rich in cattle be yours.
May Mitra sit upon our mother in front, and may he grant us strength.
The great mind that has been explained is a manifestation consisting of that very [reality] within me. (61) I raise my hand over the earth; like Indra, I do not bend down.
As the sun rises, making the stars fade, it awakens the consciousness of the entire world. (62)
O Mitra of great power, may you be our friend; O you of vast wisdom, be mindful of us. O wise Hotṛ, may you, being purified, consume this [oblation] with your mind.
O possessor of strength, bring us to sleep, for you consider [this] honey as the best.
Like Viśvāmitra and Jamadagni, may we establish our station. O Mind-made Mind, take pleasure in this of mine; let it lead us beyond intoxication.
May it not go elsewhere in vain; O Maghavan, grant us this great boon.
Wherever it may be, one beholds with that very [vision] what was previously seen;
this series of words is not merely a sequence of sounds, nor is it lacking subsequent syllables.
Adorned with qualities, composed by a knower of the Vedas, it serves as an ornament for the ears.
Furthermore, the number of *tapaḥ* rules is stated to be equal to that of *yam*. The number of *vatha* rules is stated to be equal to that of one [rule] by way of a single method;
the number of *eka* rules is stated to be equal to that of one through its being twofold. (67–68)
The enumeration of forms is thus stated as three for each [of the two], while the total number of examples is declared to be equal to the number of *maha*s (sixty-four).
Thus ends the section on *tapara*.
Having avoided what is unpraiseworthy, what is not stated, what is redundant, and having observed what is ill-reputed, even when it is near at hand.

Following the sequence of letters beginning with *ka*, I shall compose this well-structured treatise with clearly expressed meaning. [The letter] *o* at the beginning of a word, when followed by a vowel, is elided in *saṃhitā* when it occurs at the start of a word.
This treatise is composed by us in order to understand the censure [of these errors]:
"āgāt," "bhūtam," "abharaḥ," "asadat," "pādam," "eva," "ca," "agnim," "atanot," "apraḥ," "adya," "āyam," "gauḥ," "pṛśniḥ," and "akramīt. (71–72)

Ascending the mountain, he beheld the eyes of the mountain-dwelling serpents, which were dark like the pupils of his own eyes; O Agni, it is remembered that he was clearly visible within the space between their eyes. (73) And then, twenty-one threads of letters were indeed described.
And by a single method for one [deity], the number of officiating priests (ṛtvij) is thus stated;
likewise, by the duality of one, the number of forms is thus stated.
Indeed, among the sūtras numbering as many as the Vedas, only one is certain. 74–75.

Thus, one [verse] among the Bhūtasaṃkhyāka-sūtras has been proclaimed; the illustrative citation has been stated by means of an equal number of Gayas. (76) "te 'gne" (RV 8.43.24), "itthā naraḥ" (RV 1.39.7), "agniḥ suyaśaḥ" (RV 5.1.9), "agne bhānave" (RV 8.43.30), and "arca" (RV 8.44.1).
I speak to Agni; O Vasu, may those who desire you come toward us.
We praise the one who is truly red-hued. Now, we celebrate the wise ones for our prosperity. May our impulsion reach us even from yesterday; we have indeed offered our oblations.
Consuming with his ray, the man has caused [the waters] to swell for the sake of the great lord;
being born through power, he who is without enemy may protect us as we go forth against the devourers.
O Indra, there is [this] for your wrath; O slayer, O lord of horses, may it enter into us.
O wielder of the stone, the waters sang as they bore you along, O helper;
thus did the swift ones carry us home, O wise one, O dancer.
O most radiant one, you have overcome the adversaries; O Aṅgiras, you have become the greatest winner of waters.
Purifying themselves, they have come hither; the embryo is desirable; he has generated vigor, the drops.
Against us, the enemies—the Aryas and the Dāsas—have rushed forth, pressed out and through the sheep’s wool.
May glory be with us together; then, by your thought, may our seat be established this very day.
One foot of him is here in this world, O Unborn One; one foot of him is in the mountains and in the rays of light (83).
The horse of the Tumburu [wind] is the embryo within the child; Agni is two-fold; darkness is the dust, but the waters are the *sṛṇīka*.
Homage to Agni from the waters; homage to food; homage to the drinker of food (84).

You are luster, you are mind; Indra conquered the mind, and thus he conquered the out-breath, the in-breath, and the vital energies. The drops flow toward the setting sun like a bull; let the waves of honeyed milk flow forth for the cows.
The foremost waters, moving at our feet, have brought four hymns for us.
We cross over the bridge; sent by our prayer, O Indu, you who are free from malice, flow toward us with splendors for the feast of the gods, as you are released from the sheep’s wool.
Like lightning from fire, these [soma drops] are carried by the army of the gods;
he is the irresistible accomplisher of our prayers. O Agni, the lowing cows likewise flow toward you, as the wise one [the sun] looks down upon the drops and the calf, and you pervade the sheep.
O Agni, the bull rich in cattle, being praised and brought near, you are led forth even further; then the essence within the woolly fleece shines forth and becomes beautiful.
Impelled by us, being purified through the sheep’s wool, our eternal rays shine abroad.

Being praised, come toward us; at the shining forth of the waters, O hero, release for us the auspicious, ruddy ones—toward the self-powerful juice, as one free from sin. They have been let loose upon the red ones.
Protect us in the contests for booty, O Bounteous One; he is kindled with invincible [flames].
We choose, we entreat Agni; seeking him, men praise him in the Anuṣṭubh meter for aid.
In this [strife], drive away from us the godless, the virile powers, and the Aṃśus.

O Agni, for the sake of seeking cattle, we call upon you, O singer, for protection; we invoke Agni at the time of drinking for his aid. O Agni, the ruddy cows have been released; the non-givers [of gifts] are within, they desire the nectar in the house. 94. Saṃkrandana, Niṣva, Araṇa, Gāhamāna, Adaya, and likewise Yudhya—these are our arms; Anāśīrṣāṇa and Ahi are indeed the wise ones;
Marmṛjāna, Avibhiṣa, and Achāvāja are known as Netaśa. 95–96.
Furthermore, the sūtras of the vowels are clearly [determined] by the number of the earth (one) and the sky (zero);
and the twins are clearly [determined] by the number of one in a single manner. Likewise, the number of one is stated as being twofold.
The explicit citation has been clearly stated as the ninety-eighth verse:

"upa tvāgne" (1.74.1), "vijāvāgne" (6.15.13), "sāte" (6.15.19), "sumat" (6.15.20), "purāśvahayā" (10.93.11), "pūṣā bhuvat" (6.54.9), "viśvathātana" (10.158.4), and likewise "sthūṇām̐satra" (10.158.5). 98–99.
Go henceforth, O Maghavan, for you do not honor us with your greatness; since he has died, I have approached you with the brilliance of the *śukra*—you slew him by means of your magic power (*māyā*).
Sing [this] hymn! Do not act thus; come toward all the nourishments and toward the cows with your luster.
The generator of fire with his stream [produced] the waters; the upholder of cosmic order, the surging one, has entered the waters.
Thus, do thou and I come hither with sweetness, for thou shalt go to the luminous realms.
Having encompassed them, he stood beyond; they have cried out to thee together; thou hast become the head of heaven.
Through faith they move with faith; both equally, O Dakṣiṇā, you are established. By wisdom and by fire is the fire kindled.
103 O Indra, let these my prayers be for you; none indeed is equal to you in might.
O slayer of the Dasyus, you have overcome the forms [of the enemy]; O slayer of Vṛtra, you have become the supreme.
Whose praiseworthy deed has indeed been celebrated with power; you are the upholder, the one who dwells in the waters, the exhilarating slayer of Vṛtra, the friend of the horse-possessor.
The Vṛtra-slayer has struck with golden weapons; may the auspicious ones not turn away.
Through battle they have become powerful; with sweetness they have overcome all worlds, ever-moving.
106 You are the distributor by your own self; O Agni, with your army and through your protection.
The great dark one [is praised] with homage; let the high [one] be lifted up.
Like a stream of water, the King shall be further magnified for his protection, he who is victorious and never-failing.
And the bright, ruddy one is the friend of the Aśvins.

Coming at the setting of the sun with your protection, you are most ready to help; you are our father against the enemy. Fall upon the one who acts under the sway of darkness; do not let him reach us.
O slayer of demons, O King, follow after the enemies with immortality so that you may prevail.
"O gods, may you rejoice after you who are victorious; the collection of short [vowels] is complete.
(110) Thus ends the collection of short vowels. Now, the sūtras concerning the letter *ca* are proclaimed along with their total number.

And for each [verse], according to its single mode, the total number is stated thus; indeed, the sūtras here clearly amount to a number consisting of *ra*, *la*, and *gha*. Hereafter, the letter situated at the beginning of a quarter-verse (*pāda*) is taken as the [initial] syllable. 111–112.
O heroes, those who have taken hold of you, like bulls in battle, have entered the light;
we choose you as our companions for the journey. O Aśvins, grant us all life and the strength of food.
For the sake of enjoyment, he dwells among the people; this Varṇin has been well-fashioned.
(114) Come with your aid, come first, come with whiteness; come to the libations!
(115) Now, the threads of the colors have been declared according to the number of lunar days.
And the number of the sides for one [verse] is stated in that same manner by a single method.

Where an ending in long ā, an ending in circumflex (svarita), or the word following *āṅ* is seen, and where there is the augment *ūt* and the preceding *āgā*, those two Purandhrīs are extended by the Aśvins. 116–117.
"vṛṣāviśata," "śvetyāgāt," and "yuñjīmahe" [are examples].
If there should be an *ākāra* following an *āṅ*, and an *akāra* should follow it, it should be understood as "pūrvāgāt"; both "śvetyāgāt" and [the others] are likewise. 118.
Thus has been described the unimpeded attainment,
equal to the mind of a sage, churned from the ocean of the scriptures.
Salutations again and again to the risen, immortal Murāri (the enemy of Mura).

119 To Him who is devoid of the three qualities (*guṇas*), the creator of the three worlds, the eternal director of the three Vedas—to Him, the destroyer of the three cities (*Tripurāntaka*), salutations! 120
Having paid homage to the Teacher who subdues obstacles, he now instructs [his disciples];
I shall now declare the definition known as *anavagraha*.
(121) Thus ends the introductory terminology (*paribhāṣā*).

O Agni, come to the sacrifice; indeed, O Agni, come hither toward us. Truly, O Agni, [we call] upon you first. Agni for you—[the ancient one]; Agni with his sharp [flames]. Yoke [your steeds], protect us! 122 O Agni, listen! That which has been offered, O Agni—that splendor belongs to Indra.
O Indra, you who possess great strength, split the enemy; come here to our invocation.
When Indra has drunk of the Soma juices, the bull of the gods bellows. O Indra, for the sake of the one who gives, we offer praise to you, the great one. Who indeed [is equal to you]? 123–124.
Come well, O Indra, for the sake of the cattle; you are always our choice.
Indeed, the singers seek you alone, just as the wild ox seeks its herd.
For thus you are, O Indra, the one upon whom we rest; yours indeed is that which flows forth.
Come to you with the waters of Soma; that Soma has been pressed, O ancient one.
Whether it be that which you carry, O Indra—O Indra, that drop of Soma for you among the pressed juices—is this prayer and fortune indeed.
We celebrate Agni; him I consider the Brahman. Come hither now like this, O Agni, with your wood; flow forth, you who are the impeller of all.
With the sweetest [hymn], flow as Indra, the bull of all, with your stream.
Indu, the stone, flow on; O Indu, three voices arise. 129.
Resounding, you have been released like chariot-horses when you go forth; flow on, bestow wealth!
Flow on according to the ancient ways; cross over, flow for my nourishment. 130.
Flow forth, O Soma, with your exhilarating stream; O Indu, sing forth for us!
The Soma drops, being purified, have been let loose; they have been poured out, O Soma, flow on! By your impulse, you are like the great surge of the waters.
This Pūṣan is for the pressed juices; flow forth around him while being purified.
Soma has been pressed, Soma flows forth toward the bright ones;
he speeds on, the bull, for this wealth—come to all of these! 132–133.
The two bay steeds of Indra follow him; behold that splendor when it is in Agni. Truly, he has extended these lives thirtyfold; for he is the purifier.
He who is most bountiful, let him come to the hymn of the wise man; may he exult in the exhilaration of the soma.
O Soma, as a bull, flow with that [stream]; as a bull, flow for the sake of wealth. This Pūṣan has indeed sent you forth; he has released you.
Flowing while being purified, O Soma, go forward, driving away disease and bestowing long life.
Flow on with this [song], O Adhvaryu; now for Indra, the exhilarating Soma! O Indra, by what [means] will you [aid us]? O Soma, you are great; O Indra, of this [all] you are the foremost. 137.
To Indra alone, O divine Pavamāna, belong these riches; he is the one who bestows them. Agni is the leader.
"agnirjāgā tvendra yāhi yamakṣaḥ"—these are the counted [verses]. 138.
The definition of *anavagraha* (non-pause) is completed;
this treatise named *Saptalakṣaṇa* has reached its conclusion.
